title: Application Insights vs. Azure Monitor vs. Log Analytics
description: Understand the differences between Azure Monitor services and when to use each.

data.text: Azure Monitor is the umbrella platform. Application Insights is an APM service that extends Monitor for applications. Log Analytics is the data store and query engine behind Azure Monitor Logs. Together, they provide end-to-end observability.

cards.title: Azure Monitor
cards.description: The central platform collecting all telemetry from Azure resources and applications.

cards.title: Application Insights
cards.description: APM for applications with auto-instrumentation, failure analysis, and usage tracking.

cards.title: Log Analytics
cards.description: The log data store and KQL query engine for Azure Monitor Logs.

data.title: Decision Guide
items: Use Azure Monitor for infrastructure-level observability: VMs, disks, load balancers.
Use Application Insights for any application you want to monitor in detail.
Use Log Analytics when you need to store, query, and retain logs long-term.
Use all three together for a complete observability stack.

data.title: Typical Architecture
data.content: A typical web app observability setup:
data.code:
Azure App Service
  -> Application Insights (requests, exceptions, traces)
  -> Log Analytics workspace (via diagnostic settings)

Azure Monitor
  -> Metrics (CPU, memory, disk)
  -> Alerts -> Action Group (email, webhook)

data.title: Map Services to Use Cases
data.description: For each requirement, identify which Azure service(s) provide the solution.
steps: View real-time request rates for a web app.
Query 90 days of application error logs.
Get alerted when a database server runs out of disk space.
Capture a debug snapshot when a production exception occurs.
data.expectedOutcome: 1: Application Insights (Live Metrics), 2: Log Analytics (KQL), 3: Azure Monitor Metrics + Alert, 4: Application Insights (Snapshot Debugger).
